criteria.evidence: budget_required, planning_usd, critic_usd and run_usd are in config.rs. budget_reserve now calls them and keeps no sum of its own. criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: a new test parses a config with job_usd below the reserve and fails with an error naming job_usd and the shortfall; the same test fails when the check is removed, and a config at exactly the reserve parses.
criteria.evidence: job_usd_below_the_reserve_is_refused_by_the_budget_check passed. findings.summary: admission.rs changed but is not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: The expected deliverables list config.rs, reading.rs and CHANGELOG.md only. The planned files did include admission.rs, and the change there (calling check_budget when an athena.toml change is admitted, plus a test) is what connects the new check to the place config changes come in. It adds no unrelated scope.

findings.summary: The budget check runs at admission, not when config is loaded, so an athena.toml edited by hand outside Athena is caught only by the runtime preflight.
findings.evidence: check_budget is called only in admission.rs; Config::parse does not call it. The CHANGELOG says this on purpose: past commits' files must stay readable when history is walked, and runtime preflight still guards running jobs. A later improvement could call check_budget where the head config is loaded for a new job, for example in a startup warning.

summary: The change passes. It adds Config::budget_required, which sums the reader cap, max_rounds planner+critic rounds (only when [job_plan] is enabled), and the producer and verifier caps. It also adds Config::check_budget, which refuses a job_usd below that sum and names the shortfall. Admission now runs check_budget whenever an athena.toml change is admitted. budget_reserve in reading.rs now gets every stage sum from the Config helpers, so a second hand-written sum no longer exists. The CHANGELOG names the root cause and the three earlier jobs. I ran the new tests in athena-data and athena-core, the existing stage-reserve test and the admission tests: all pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full-suite checks also pass. There are two minor findings. First, admission.rs changed but is not on the expected deliverables list, though the plan included it and it is the file that connects the check to the place config changes come in. Second, the check runs at admission and not inside Config::parse, so an athena.toml edited by hand outside Athena is still caught only by the runtime preflight. The CHANGELOG says this and explains why: past commits' files must stay readable when history is walked.
